answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can earn rewards, then slash that stake when independently sampled work fails verification. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund every extra identity, and cannot cheaply copy one credential across a swarm; splitting stake also reduces each identity’s influence. The lock is like a quartz marker on an island dune: visible commitment, not proof of honesty, so sampling and penalties remain essential. The attacker pays capital costs and risks losing it.
